messages.body_plain:
Can you try str(y) right around there? Maybe there's a surprising type in that variable or something?

You can also try setting options(shiny.trace=TRUE) before launching the app, that'll let you spy on the traffic being sent back and forth.

_____________________________
From: Wayne Haythorn <wayne.h...@gmail.com>
Sent: Thursday, April 30, 2015 5:04 PM
Subject: passing values to updateNumericInput
To: <shiny-...@googlegroups.com>

I have a numericInput, and I cannot understand how its value is set by updateNumericInput.  I'll show you the code that I don't understand, and then explain it.  The code looks like this:

 observe({modelPNRR <<- input$modelPNRR

     if (modelPNRR) {

              enableActionButton("getPNRR", session)

               enableActionButton("pnrrAdj", session)

      } else {

              disableActionButton("getPNRR", session)

              disableActionButton("pnrrAdj", session)

     }

})

observe({pnrrAdjustment <<- input$pnrrAdj})

observe({if (modelPNRR && input$getPNRR > 0) {

     # start a progress message

     y <- getPNRR(.95)

     print(paste("value returned for pnrr is ", y))

     updateNumericInput(session, "pnrrAdj", value = y)

     # updateNumericInput(session, "pnrrAdj", value = 25)      # this updates the value

})

The modelPNRR variable turns this part of the program off and on, so input$modelPNRR is a checkbox.  When it is checked, the program uses a variable called pnrrAdjustment, which can be set by the user, or calculated.  So modelPNRR enables a numericInput (input$pnrrAdj) for the user to set the value, and also enables an action button (input$getPNRR)

pnrrAdjustment is defined in the environment of the server function. The getPNRR function calculates and sets its value, and returns the value set.  The calculation is iterative, so it is set multiple times during the getPNRR call.  In the code shown, the updateNumericInput call fails - the value is not set in the input control, but the observe on input$pnrrAdj is apparently being triggered, because the pnrrAdjustment variable in my program is being set to NA.  print statement is showing the right value, and the updateNumericInput call that I've commented out does set a value.

I feel like this must be something simple that I am unable to see.

--

messages.subject: Leaflet conflict with shinydashboard?
messages.subject_clean: Leaflet conflict with shinydashboard?
messages.body_plain:
The MRE below displays some odd behavior:

- Run as-is, it displays two valueBoxOutput on the good ol mtcars dataset

- However, if we uncomment the renderLeaflet function at the end of the server block (lines 46 - 49), the valueBoxOutputs disappear AND the map fails to render

Any diagnosis is appreciated.

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)
library(leaflet)
library(magrittr)
library(dplyr)

mycars <- mtcars

## Assign some random coordinates to mtcars to draw on a map
mycars$lon <- runif(n_distinct(rownames(mtcars)), min = -110, max = -80)
mycars$lat <- runif(n_distinct(rownames(mtcars)), min = 30, max = 45)

ui <-  dashboardPage(
        dashboardHeader(title = "mtcars"),
        dashboardSidebar(),
        dashboardBody(
          fluidRow(
            valueBoxOutput("count"),
            valueBoxOutput("disp")
            ),
          fluidRow(
            box(
              width = 9, status = "info", solidHeader = TRUE,
              title = "Property Map",
              leafletOutput("myMap")
            )
         )
))

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$count <- renderValueBox({
    valueBox(
      value = n_distinct(rownames(mtcars)),
      subtitle = "# cars",
      color = "blue"
    )
  })

  output$disp <- renderValueBox({
    valueBox(
      value = sum(mtcars$disp, na.rm = TRUE),
      subtitle = "Total displacement",
      color = "green"
    )
  })
#   output$myMap <- renderLeaflet({
#     leaflet(mycars) %>% addTiles() %>% addCircleMarkers()
#   })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)

Eventually I want to plot different x-y data using the data.frame that was loaded, but I want to choose the specific x-y data variables since it will be different for each .csv data.frame I load.

Please see my ui.R and server.R files below that show what I was trying to do.  I am also attaching an example .csv file that it the app will require to run.   I would like to see the displayed table change it's columns depending on the choices that are made, and eventually write code that will plot one variable against another after I have selected them.  I took example code from the following 2 examples, since it looks like I just need to "combine" these 2 examples:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/blob/master/009-upload/ui.R
https://gist.github.com/wch/4211337

Thanks in advance for any suggestions.

Kevin

ui.R

library(googleVis)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel(""),

  sidebarPanel(

    #create file upload control
    fileInput('file1','Choose CSV File',
              accept=c('text/csv',
                       'text/comma-separated-values,text/plain',
                       '.csv')),
    tags$hr(),

    #create check box control to decide whether to include header
    checkboxInput('header', 'Header', TRUE),

    #use radio button control to decide the type of sepator in the file
    radioButtons('sep', 'Separator',
                 c(Comma=',',
                   Semicolon=';',
                   Tab='\t'),
                 ','),

    #use radio button control to decide the type of quotes in the file
    radioButtons('quote', 'Quote',
                 c(None='',
                   'Double Quote'='"',
                   'Single Quote'="'"),
                 '"')

  ),

  mainPanel(

    htmlOutput('contents'),
    uiOutput("choose_columns")

  )
))

server.R

library(googleVis)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$contents <- renderGvis({

    inFile <- input$file1

    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)

  #load file that was specified by user and save into a uploaded data frame
  upload.data=read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep,
                       quote=input$quote)

  # Check boxes
  output$choose_columns <- renderUI({

    colnames <- names(upload.data)

    # Create the checkboxes and select them all by default
    checkboxGroupInput("columns", "Choose columns",
                       choices  = colnames,
                       selected = colnames)

  })

  ## Output the uploaded data into a google table chart

  gvisTable(head(upload.data))

  })

})

sudo update-rc.d apache2 disable

On Friday, March 6, 2015 at 2:59:30 AM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> OK, let's take a step back.
>
> You have both Apache and Shiny Server configured to listen on port 80. That is certainly not going to work. I think the first question is whether you actually need Apache for anything. The simplest would be to shut down Apache (or configure it to stop listening on port 80, and reload) and restart Shiny Server, and I think that should start working.
>
> If you do need to have Apache listening on port 80 (for example if you have other web stuff you are serving using other URL paths on the same host/port) then what you want to do is not serve up a <Directory>, but rather, proxy that traffic through to Shiny Server. To do this, change Shiny Server back to listening on port 3838 and remove the server_name directive, then set ProxyPass <http://httpd.apache.org/docs/current/mod/mod_proxy.html#proxypass> and ProxyPassReverse <http://httpd.apache.org/docs/current/mod/mod_proxy.html#proxypassreverse> directives in your Apache config. Probably something like this:
>
> ProxyPass / http://127.0.0.1:3838/
> ProxyPassReverse / http://127.0.0.1:3838/
>
> If that doesn't work, first try viewing port 3838 from inside the firewall to see if the Shiny Server instance is even working. If that works, then check the Apache logs to see why the proxying is failing.
>

messages.subject: Heatmap Not Displaying on Shiny App Load
messages.subject_clean: Heatmap Not Displaying on Shiny App Load
messages.body_plain:
Greetings fellow Shiny useRs!

I have been working on an app to display mouse neuroanatomical data clustered by mouse strain.  I've greatly simplified the app for the purposes of explaining it here and creating a reproducible example.  Basically, all the map is is a heatmap.  The problem is, during some point when I was coding the app, the heatmap stopped showing up on the first page of the app when I'd launch it locally in my browser, and I'd have to resize the window in order for the heatmap to show up properly.  Since I'm relatively stumped, I've created what I believe to be a reproducible example with the hope that an expert can help me out:

ui.R

shinyUI(
  navbarPage('Menu',

             tabPanel('Filter and Recluster',

                      titlePanel('Blah'),

                      p('Blah'),

                      hr(),

                      fluidRow(column(12, plotOutput(outputId = 'heatmap1', height = "800px"))),

                      hr(),

                      fluidRow(
                        column(4, checkboxInput(inputId = 'selectAllStrains',
                                                label = 'Select/Deselect All Strains',
                                                value = TRUE)),
                        column(4, checkboxInput(inputId = 'selectAllRegions',
                                                label = 'Select/Deselect All Regions',
                                                value = TRUE))
                      ),

                      hr(),

                      fluidRow(
                        column(4, uiOutput('selectStrains')),
                        column(4, uiOutput('selectRegions')),
                        column(4, actionButton('recalculate', 'Recalculate'))
                      )

             ),

             tabPanel('Plot Means and Effect Sizes',

                      hr()
             )
  )
)

server.R

jdfs = function(x) {
  as.dist(1-cor(t(x)))
}

shinyServer(
  function(input, output) {

    # Page 1 dynamic control - select all brain regions
    output$selectRegions = renderUI({
      if (input$selectAllRegions == TRUE) {
        checkboxGroupInput(inputId = 'regions',
                           label = h3('Brain Regions'),
                           choices = sort(colnames(testdatadf)),
                           selected = colnames(testdatadf))
      } else {
        checkboxGroupInput(inputId = 'regions',
                           label = h3('Brain Regions'),
                           choices = sort(colnames(testdatadf)),
                           selected = vector(mode="character", length=0))
      }
    })

    # Page 1 dynamic control - select all mouse strains
    output$selectStrains = renderUI({
      if (input$selectAllStrains == TRUE) {
        checkboxGroupInput(inputId = 'strains',
                           label = h3('Mouse Strains'),
                           choices = sort(rownames(testdatadf)),
                           selected = rownames(testdatadf))
      } else {
        checkboxGroupInput(inputId = 'strains',
                           label = h3('Mouse Strains'),
                           choices = sort(rownames(testdatadf)),
                           selected = vector(mode="character", length=0))
      }
    })

    # Page 1 plot - heatmap for reclustering
    output$heatmap1 = renderPlot({
      input$recalculate

      # isolate() prevents heatmap from regenerating every time a new strain/region is selected
      testdatadfmat = as.matrix(testdatadf[isolate(input$strains), isolate(input$regions)])
      nr = dim(testdatadfmat)[1]
      nc = dim(testdatadfmat)[2]

      if (dim(testdatadfmat)[1] > 1 & dim(testdatadfmat)[2] > 1) {
        heatmap.2(x=testdatadfmat,
                  distfun=jdfs,
                  #hclustfun=hclust.avg,
                  col=bluered,
                  margins=c(20,14),
                  trace='none',
                  cexRow=1.5,
                  cexCol=1.5,
                  density.info='histogram',
                  keysize=0.8,
                  symkey=TRUE,
                  symbreaks=TRUE)
      }
    }, height=800)

  }
)

global.R

require(gplots)
require(shiny)

# simulate mousedata
testdata = rep(x=-5:5, each=1, times=10)
testdatadf = as.data.frame(matrix(testdata, nrow=10, ncol=10))

Please excuse the awkward indentation in these files -- I haven't found a robust tool yet to automatically indent R code (formatR unfortunately doesn't work for Shiny code as far as I know).

Basically, when you launch this app from a directory using:

runApp(appDir=<directory containing the above files>, launch.browser=TRUE)

The plot will not immediately show up on the first page, yet, if you press Recalculate or resize the window in the horizontal dimension the plot will show up.  I have determined that if I comment out the following lines in ui.R:

                      titlePanel('Blah'),

                      p('Blah'),

                      hr(),

Then the plot magically shows up again without having the manually click the Recalculate button or resize the window.  Any idea why this would be the case?

messages.subject: General Debugging Tips for Developing Shiny Apps
messages.subject_clean: General Debugging Tips for Developing Shiny Apps
messages.body_plain:
Hey Shiny useRs!

I have a number of questions which I think would be useful for other people testing their apps if there were answers to these particular questions.  Without further ado:
It's difficult to predict how the styling will appear for a given app depending on the device/program with which you view it.  I've had occasions where firefox displays a checkboxGroupInput diagonally whereas this other browser (rekonq) displays a checkboxGroupInput vertically, and other odd behaviour, and it's just hard to predict what's going on here.  Another example is that shinyAppDir('/TestAppDir/') produces different styling than runApp(appDir='/TestAppDir/', launch.browser=TRUE) -- checkboxGroupInput boxes appear as X's for the former command whereas they appear as checks for the latter command.
Is there a way of changing the default browser that the app launches on if you run the app from RStudio?
How would you recommend testing in various browsers simultaneously?  There are tools like browserstack <http://www.browserstack.com>, which I haven't used, but I imagine there are other best practices out there to make shiny apps appear nicely on as many browsers as possible.
How does the control flow actually work when a Shiny app is launched (namely, the communication between server.R, ui.R, and global.R)?
When you make a change to code in ui.R or server.R, and then immediately relaunch the app, sometimes those changes don't immediately take effect, and you have to wait an indeterminate amount of time for the changes to be displayed.  Is there a way of speeding up the process of: modify code -> test app -> wait -> test app -> wait -> ... -> test app -> result?
Are there any supplementary resources beyond this one <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/debugging.html> on general best practices for debugging Shiny apps?
Is there more comprehensive Shiny documentation than that found at http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles?  In general the documentation is very good, I'm just wondering if there are any books or anything.

In general Shiny has been quite easy to pick up and it's pretty fun, I just want the community to get the most from it as possible :)

messages.subject: Re: General Debugging Tips for Developing Shiny Apps
messages.subject_clean: General Debugging Tips for Developing Shiny Apps
messages.body_plain:
1 & 3: For things like "x" versus check boxes, unless you want to become a professional web designer I suggest you try to get used to it--the cost of fixing and debugging such issues across all browsers is enormous and getting higher with each new platform that gets popular. I'm surprised to hear shinyAppDir(...) is different than runApp(...), unless those two are launching different browsers (perhaps the former is the RStudio preview window, while the latter is your system's default web browser?). And I'm also surprised to hear that Firefox displays checkboxGroupInput diagonally--can you send a screenshot of that?

2: You can call option(shiny.launch.browser = function(url) { ... }) where the function you're passing in launches the given URL in the web browser of your choice (probably using system()). Or just change your system's default web browser, and from the "Run App" toolbar button's menu, select "Run External".

4. global.R is run when the app is launched (i.e. no user has arrived yet), and it executes in the global environment. The shinyUI in ui.R is generally run once, and the results are saved; all this does is generate HTML which is served to any browser that arrives at the Shiny app's root URL. One of the things that HTML does is attempt to connect to the server using a websocket; when it does so, that's when the shinyServer function in server.R is executed.

5. I've never observed this. How much time are you needing to wait? What operating system are you using? What version of RStudio?

6. There are some slides on debugging here: https://speakerdeck.com/jcheng5/advanced-shiny (see slides 6-10)

7. We're strongly considering writing one. In the meantime there's one book by Packt Press that I know of: https://www.packtpub.com/web-development/web-application-development-r-using-shiny

messages.body_plain:
You don't want to convert to GeoJSON; instead, you want to use the sp package to create a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame, that joins together the polygon geometry with the data. SpatialPolygonsDataFrame makes it easy to filter the polygons based on year.

So imagine you formed the SpatialPolygonsDataFrame and called it `spdf`:

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  # Create a continuous color palette that maps spdf$Frequency to the
  # ColorBrewer2.org palette "RdYlBu"
  pal <- colorNumeric("RdYlBu", range(spdf$Frequency))

  # This reactive will filter the spdf by year
  spdfYear <- reactive({
    spdf[spdf$Year == input$year,]
  })

# Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
run_as shiny;

# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
  listen 3838 "serverIP";
  server_name "shiny.mydomain.com <http://shiny.mydomain.com>";

  # Define a location at the base URL
  location / {

    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server;

    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;

    # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
    # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
    directory_index on;
  }
}

# ui.R

  titlePanel("Google StreetView"),

    AndrewMap <- gvisMap(Andrew, "LatLong" , "Tip",
                         options=list(showTip=TRUE,
                                      showLine=TRUE,
                                      enableScrollWheel=TRUE,
                                      mapType='terrain',
                                      useMapTypeControl=TRUE)),
    plot(AndrewMap)
  )
))

Hi All,

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: Heatmap Not Displaying on Shiny App Load
messages.subject_clean: Heatmap Not Displaying on Shiny App Load
messages.body_plain:
The problem is that the initial values of input$strains and input$regions are NULL, because they are dynamic UI.

And because you have them in isolate(), when these values do get updated, they don't cause the plot to get redrawn. (What does cause the plot to redraw when you resize is an implicit dependence on the height and width of the plotting region. More info on that at http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/client-data.html)

If you put this code inside your renderPlot code, you'll see the NULL values:
    isolate({
      print(input$strains)
      print(input$regions)
    })

What you want is for the renderPlot() to take a dependency on input$strains and input$regions when they're NULL, and then to drop that dependency when they're not NULL.

Adding these to the renderPlot() should do the trick:
    if (is.null(isolate(input$strains)))
      validate(need(input$strains, FALSE))
    if (is.null(isolate(input$regions)))
      validate(need(input$regions, FALSE))

The validate(need()) part checks for a valid value, and exits the function if it's not valid (e.g. NULL or FALSE).

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
I'm not sure what you mean by "use them step by step" but the idiomatic way to do this, if you need to access the intermediate values, is to use a different reactive for each step.

df <- ...

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  subsetted <- reactive({
    validate(need(input$columns, "Please choose some columns"))
    df[,input$columns]
  })
  reshaped <- reactive({
    melt(subsetted(), ...)  # or whatever
  })
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot2(reshaped(), ...)  # or whatever
  })
})

messages.subject: Re: Configure Apache with shiny-server
messages.subject_clean: Configure Apache with shiny-server
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

you are running two servers:

- The shiny server which listens at shiny.mydomain.com <http://shiny.mydomain.com/>:3838, so I guess http://shiny.mydomain.com <http://shiny.mydomain.com/>:3838/App1 will work.
- The Apache webserver listens at shiny.mydomain.com <http://shiny.mydomain.com/>:80. Accessing http://shiny.mydomain.com <http://shiny.mydomain.com/>/App1 will access the directory /var/www/shiny/App1 and if it does not exists or it is empty you will get an error message.

If you want to access your shiny App with http://shiny.mydomain.com <http://shiny.mydomain.com/>/App1 then the Apache server must redirect http://shiny.mydomain.com <http://shiny.mydomain.com/>/App1 to http://shiny.mydomain.com <http://shiny.mydomain.com/>:3838/App1 which can be done with the Proxy directive; you posted in the thread where it is described.

Best Sigbert

messages.subject: passing UI inputs to ggvis plot object
messages.subject_clean: passing UI inputs to ggvis plot object
messages.body_plain:
I'd like to generate overlapping histograms based on user-selected variables in the UI.  Below is a toy MRE with three variables in the df and in the checkboxGroupInput.
Ideally, the resulting plot would have 3,2,1, or zero overlapping histogram bars, depending on the user selection.  I've also attached a sample image of what the overlapping histogram might look like.

the code:
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(ggvis)

# some play data
my_df <- data.frame(rock = runif(100, 0, 20), paper = runif(100, 10, 25), scissors = runif(100, 0 , 25))

ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(
  checkboxGroupInput("attr", label = "Attribute", choices = c("rock", "paper", "scissors"), selected = c("rock", "paper"),
  ggvisOutput("plot1")
)))

server <-  shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  vis <- reactive({ # following the form of the move explorer example in the shiny gallery
    xvar <- prop("x", as.symbol(input$attr))

    my_df %>% ggvis(xvar) %>%  layer_histograms(fill := "yellow")
#    my_df %>% ggvis(xvar[2]) %>%  layer_histograms(fill := "blue") #this doesn't work
#    my_df %>% ggvis(xvar[3]) %>%  layer_histograms(fill := "green") #nor this
  })
  vis %>% bind_shiny("plot1")
})

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

to the SO post?). On the contrary, I'd recommend you to avoid C. You
current locale en_US.UTF-8 is better at handling non-ASCII characters,
so what we really need to do is to fix the DataTables issue, which has
probably gone with the new DT package (http://rstudio.github.io/DT/)
but I can certainly try to fix the to-be-deprecated versions of
renderDataTable()/dataTableOutput() in shiny.

Regards,
Yihui

The issue is, when I enter a string into the filter box (any string - no special characters), I get this error in shiny:

Error in tolower(x) : invalid multibyte string 664

DataTables warning: table id=DataTables_Table_2 - Ajax error. For more information about this error, please see http://datatables.net/tn/7

These errors do not occur when the locale='C' option is used.

It looks like shiny is trying to convert the table data to lowercase to enable case insensitive matching, but it's choking on some odd characters in the data table.

messages.subject: More attractive printing from Shiny in Windows Chrome browser?
messages.subject_clean: More attractive printing from Shiny in Windows Chrome browser?
messages.body_plain:
I was wondering if anyone had suggestions on better looking output for printing Shiny output from the brower to a printer, on Windows.

My Shiny App uses a typical sidebarLayout with a sidebarPanel and a mainPanel. If Shiny runs from RStudio, the App runs as expected, but you can't print the page.

So, when I runApp( launch.browser = TRUE),

- on my Mac in Safari, the Shiny App displays beautifully, and prints out as expected

- on the hospital Windows workstation, if the system's default browser is Internet Explorer, it fails (not compatible with Shiny I guess)

- on the hospital Windows workstation, if the system's default browser is changed to Chrome, the output looks fine in Chrome, but when you print it, the sidebar and main panels are no longer side-by-side; this is unsightly, but the nurses need paper

So I actually have 2 questions:

1) how do you get a sidebar / main panel output to print out nicely in Windows?

2) is it possible when using runApp(launch.browser = TRUE) to select which browser is started? The hospital will not take kindly to my changing the default browser on multiple workstations

Thanks for any tips.

Joe

I am trying to load a graphic generated after a somewhat lengthy calculation. Most of the time it works but sometimes I get an Error: Replacement length zero. The calculation is to generate a dataframe to conduct a 2d histogram. This never happens when I run the code on its own, only when it's presented in a Shiny app. Here's the code to trigger the function:

     output$clustersShow <- renderPlot({
       if(input$clusterButton > 0) {
         clust.size <- input$clusterSlider
         numTraces <-30
         list_df <- makeClusters(numTraces)
         df1     <- list_df[[1]]
         drops     <- c("Trace")
         df1.clust <- df1[,!(names(df1) %in% drops)]
         df1C            <- bestCluster(df1.clust, clust.size, df1)
         df1C$clusterCat <- factor(df1C$Cluster)

         plot.cats       <- ggplot(df1C, aes(x=Noise, y = AvgC), colour=clusterCat) + geom_point( aes(color=clusterCat, size=4))
         plot.cats

       }
     })

It's makeClusters() that takes a while. I don't see this fitting into the isolate() or reactive() functions, but perhaps I am missing something. How can I get renderPlot to defer presenting the view until makeClusters() and subsequent functions return?

messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to create a Shiny version of a console program that I've written (genetic algorithm demonstration).

Currently, when an actionButton is pressed the program does lots of processing inside a loop, then outputs a graph. That works fine.

What I'd like to do is have the processing loop create a block of HTML output that will change with each iteration. Once complete the graph should be displayed.

I've created simple skeleton code below to demonstrate what I'm trying to do. It fails to display any text, producing an error message saying:
>
> Error in func() : object 'h' not found

Could someone please point me in the right direction?

Thank you.
app <- shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    fluidRow(  actionButton("go", "Go!") ),

    fluidRow(htmlOutput("html")),

    fluidRow(plotOutput('plot'))
 ),

server = function(input, output) {

  myPlot <- eventReactive(input$go, {

    for (i in 1:5){
      h <- HTML("some text to be displayed")

      cat(i) # outputs to the console, just for debugging

      Sys.sleep(1) # pause for 1 second
    }

    hist(runif(15))
  })

  output$html <- renderUI({ h }) # This doesn't produce any output

  output$plot <- renderPlot({ myPlot() }) # This displays a graph after the loop terminates
})

runApp(app)

messages.subject: 80/20 Rule Applied to Open Source Shiny Server Security
messages.subject_clean: 80/20 Rule Applied to Open Source Shiny Server Security
messages.body_plain:
Hello all.  Let me describe my scenario / use case.

I have an Apache server running as a reverse proxy to the open source version of Shiny server.  My use case is for research, specifically to allow researchers to collaborate and openly share data.  There isn't any sensitive data in my app (e.g. financial information, personal health information), however, I still want to take the necessary precautions in securing the Shiny server to prevent it from being hijacked.  There are obviously guides for securing an Apache server, which I am going through before making my app public, but even if my Apache server is secure, my understanding is that my Shiny server could still potentially be exploited if there are vulnerabilities.  In particular, I am interested in expending 20% of the effort to make my server 80% safe, since I am quite busy, as I imagine many others on this forum are as well.

Has anyone went through this process and is also willing to give some tips on securing an Apache + Shiny server combo?

Do any guides exist for securing a Shiny server?

What are the most important quick and dirty tips for securing an Apache + Shiny Server combo?

At some point I might want to implement users/passwords/authentication, which I see there have been some posts on this topic already on this forum.  What has worked for people using this model?

Thanks!  I hope this can help serve the community as a quick guide to (mostly) securing a private Shiny Server.

messages.subject: Re: Unknown job: shiny-server

messages.body_plain:
Just to update - I hit the same problem on a fresh install of shiny-server on mint 17.1, and upstart won't work.

/etc/init/shiny-server.conf does not exist at the end of the install. After a quick glance at the documentation, I realised /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf did exist, and copied it over. But even though they have the same name, these are two different files. shiny-server looks at /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf when starting, and this file is correctly formatted, as evidenced by the ability to start the server on the command line.

Upstart looks at /etc/init/shiny-server.conf before starting it. Clearly, copying it over was the wrong thing to do, because upstart just complained it was improperly formated, it needed the fix documented above.

Thanks

Jeff.

messages.subject: updateActionButton
messages.subject_clean: updateActionButton
messages.body_plain:
I know this is a long-standing issue, and I know that Joe Cheng always maintains that desires for updateActionButton are misguided, in that that there is a proper way to achieve desired functionality without it.

However, I don't find the following functionality discussed explicitly so far, so I'll try it out.  It has to do with using a conditional panel that looks at an action button value for its condition (this is in ui.R, *not* server.R).

In a sidePanel I have something like:

sidePanel(...
actionButton(doit,"Configure this variable")
...
)

then in a main panel I have something like

mainPanel(   ...
   # for action button not pushed:
   conditionalPanel(condition="input.doit == 0 & input.tabs==...",
                                ...),
   ...
   # for action button pushed:
   conditionalPanel(condition="input.doit > 0 & input.tabs==...",
                                ...),

Now, at some later point (maybe triggered by another action button), I would like to reset input.doit and re-display the first conditional panel, have the user re-specify inputs there, etc.  Seems like it would be quite natural to have something like updateActionButton() over in server.R to get me back to my first conditional panel.

I would be very happy to hear the 'right and proper' way to do this, given that  updateActionButton() does not exist.  Very sorry if I have missed the solution in previous discussions.

messages.body_plain:
OK. Manage to hack it.

I add one more line in the click() function in simpleNetwork.js to send Shiny.onInputChange back to Shiny. The click() is now something like this:

    // click event handler
    function click(d) {
      d3.select(this).select("text").transition()
        .duration(750)
        .attr("x", 22)
        .style("stroke-width", ".5px")
        .style("opacity", 1)
        .style("fill", x.options.nodeClickColour)
        .style("font", x.options.clickTextSize + "px serif");
      d3.select(this).select("circle").transition()
        .duration(750)
        .style("fill", x.options.nodeClickColour)
        .attr("r", 16);

 Shiny.onInputChange(el.id <http://el.id>+"_clickednode", d.name <http://d.name>); ## added line to send onInputChange back to Shiny.
    }

Let me know if there is a more elegant way. :)

Cheers,

JS

Jürgen

messages.subject: Responsive breakpoints in fluidrow
messages.subject_clean: Responsive breakpoints in fluidrow
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone:

Is there a way to assign a breakpoint such that the elements in `fluidRow` will respond at a given browser width?

I am working on an app using shinydashboard and the `box` widget.
The problem is when I have 3 `box` elements in a `fluidRow` with the `width=4` the box reflow too late,
and there is an awkward period where the contents of the `box` begin to look too squished.

I believe the proper way to do this is to use CSS media querries, but I cannot seem to get the settings correct.
I should be able to add a `class` element to the `box` or `fluidRow` and have different CSS elements in the header as follows:

    singleton(tags$head(tags$link(rel='stylesheet',
                                            media='(max-width: 700)',
                                            href='screen_narrow.css',
                                            type='text/css')))

Do I assign a CSS rule to the `fluidRow` or to the `box` element?

I believe the other way is to have some kind of reactive client-server-client variable that will assign the `width` parameter in `box` to 4 if the browser is wide, and 12 if it meets some threshold width.

Thanks for the help,
Dan

messages.body_plain:
You can write a helper function to do it, e.g.

read.table2 = function(file) {
  files = input$files
  file = files$datapath[files$name == file]
  read.csv(file)
}

Then you read.table2('1.txt')

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: Responsive breakpoints in fluidrow
messages.subject_clean: Responsive breakpoints in fluidrow
messages.body_plain:
You can try using custom container classes using the "Grid system" section of http://getbootstrap.com/css/ as a guide, for example:

div(class="col-md-3 col-sm-4",
   ...
)

for a div that would take 3/12 of the available width on desktop browsers, 4/12 of the width for tablets, and 12/12 for phones.

Sent from Outlook <http://taps.io/outlookmobile>

messages.subject: shiny no longer responds to button clicks after 2 submits, when a legend is attached to leaflet map
messages.subject_clean: shiny no longer responds to button clicks after 2 submits, when a legend is attached to leaflet map
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am encountering a rather strange problem in the integration of shiny and leaflet:

I am using an action button input$queryExec to trigger the query of data and rendering of map. Each time this button is clicked, the map adjusted accordingly. However, if I add a legend to the map, then after exactly 2 button clicks (or 2 submits) based on whatever selection criteria, shiny does not react any more. The leaflet widget remain working, but it is no longer updated accordingly. I also added a print statement for the button to debug at runtime, but after 2 clicks nothing is printed. It means shiny no longer receives the value change of the button. Here is part of the code:

>   results <- reactive({
>     input$queryExec
>     if (input$queryExec > 0) {
>       sumResults <- SPARQL(endpoint, isolate(filteredQuery()), curl_args=list(userpwd="rstudio:rstudio", httpauth=TRUE))$results
>       sumResults <- data.frame(refArea = sumResults[, 1], num = sumResults[, 2])
>       sumResults
>     }
>   })
>   output$map <- renderLeaflet({
>     m <- leaflet() %>%
>       addTiles() %>%
>       fitBounds(6.333618, 49.484186, 2.510375, 51.476251)
>
> # leave out some manipulations
>
>       m %>%
>         addPolygons(data = polygons,
>                     fillColor = pal(newObsVal),
>                     fillOpacity = 0.8,
>                     color = "#BDBDC3",
>                     weight = 1,
>                     popup = popup) %>%
>         addLegend(pal = palLegend, values = bins, position = 'bottomright', title = NULL) %>%
>         clearBounds()
>     }
>
>   })

If I remove the statement "addLegend", the application will work properly. Then it will always respond, whatever the selection criteria is. So I wonder the problem is from the leaflet side and it should not be my responsibilty :D

Before opening a new issue at the leaflet github repo, I would like to post this question here and see if it is a bug of leaflet or a bug of myself. :D Has anybody else encountered such type of issue? Any help is appreciated. Thank you very much in advance and have a nice day!

Regards,
Yang

messages.subject: Re: updateActionButton
messages.subject_clean: updateActionButton
messages.body_plain:
Andrew, not sure why your actionLink isn't working inside a uiOutput/renderUI, it certainly should.

Norman, that's a good one :) Most of the other instances have purely involved juggling state on the server, the conditionalPanel means we have to communicate the state back to the client.

I might be thawing a bit on updateActionButton but in the meantime here's how you would do it without it:

mainPanel(   ...
   # for action button not pushed:

   conditionalPanel(condition="!output.hideinputs && input.tabs==...",

                                ...),
   ...
   # for action button pushed:

   conditionalPanel(condition="output.hideinputs && input.tabs==...",
                                ...),

(By the way, I noticed you used single & for boolean-AND, that's not correct for JavaScript--you need &&.)

Then on the server:

function(input, output, session) {
  # These two lines are a way to create a single reactive value variable
  hideinputs <- FALSE
  makeReactiveBinding("hideinputs")

  observeEvent(input$doit, {
    hideinputs <- TRUE
  })
  observeEvent(input$reset, { # or whatever
    hideinputs <- FALSE
  })

  # These two lines take the value of hideinputs and make it available
  # in the client as output.hideinputs. It's a little verbose, we should
  # probably have a convenience function for this.
  output$hideinputs <- reactive(hideinputs)
  outputOptions(output, "hideinputs", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
}

This would have a disadvantage versus updateActionButton in that the controls wouldn't hide until the output is ready (since the value of output.hideinputs isn't updated until all the other outputs are ready to update as well).

messages.subject: Shiny testing - best practices and advice
messages.subject_clean: Shiny testing - best practices and advice
messages.body_plain:
Our company uses several shiny apps which we have written, both on our own servers and using the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> service.

We are trying to put in place automated testing for these. At an absolute minimum we would like to know that the right app is running at the right URL, and that it loads correctly (not greyed out on load, no error console). Ideally we would like to check much more - for example we want to click through all tabs to see that they load correctly, do some basic input, and check the output. We want to know about both bugs in our code or infrastructure problems such as incorrect database details before our customers do.

We have started writing selenium tests, both with RSelenium and selenium for Python. However we have found that writing good Selenium tests is tricky, and that a lot of work has to be done to get tests which are reasonably stable, and which give us meaningful results. Some of this seems to the normal work that Selenium requires to be used (ie finding all the right CSS selectors and checking the DOM after each UI interaction to check for elements which might have moved/disappeared/been replaced). Some of it seems to be related to the complexity of our pages and the Shiny UI elements, and some of it we think is unexpected behavior by Selenium. One example is that we have found it impossible in RSelenium to correctly interact with the Selectize Bootstrap widget in Shiny.

Is Selenium the best approach and is RSelenium the best others have found to test Shiny? Is there anything that we should know about when trying to write Selenium tests for Shiny code? Should we change how we write our app code to make Selenium testing work better?

I would be very happy to here from anyone who has any suggestions or can share there experiences, particularly if they have been successful in doing extensive automated testing of Shiny apps.

Thanks ia,
Jack Grahl

messages.subject_clean: Laggy uiOutput("plot.ui")
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

One of my apps is displaying a ggplot via uiOutput('plot.ui') and plot.ui is rendered through renderUI().

output$plot.ui=renderUI({
plotOutput('plot', width=a function(), height=a function())
})

The code works, but it is very laggy. It seems that this is a two-step process. In my app, it first renders 'plot' (which is a ggplot rendered by renderPlot), then it resizes the plot according the specified width and height. The lag between the two steps is significant (about 3 seconds). I checked it by wrapping a withProgress() around plotOutput(), and the problem still exists. I am wondering why this problem exists and if there is any way to solve it.

Thank you very much for your help!

messages.subject: Enabling Case-Insensitive Domain Names on Shiny-Server
messages.subject_clean: Enabling Case-Insensitive Domain Names on Shiny-Server
messages.body_plain:
Hi all.

Let's say you've configured a private shiny-server and have an app running on it.  The app is accessible when you type in the exact same string as that found in your site_dir, which is a directive specified in /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf.  The problem with this is that the app address is case-sensitive.

Let's say you've chosen the default settings and have apps hosted in /srv/shiny-server.  If you have an app located in /srv/shiny-server/MyApp, if you enter 127.0.0.1/myapp <http://127.0.0.1/myapp>, the address will not resolve.  What would you recommend to make the url more stable in terms of case-sensitivity?  I couldn't find anything in the admin guide.

Thanks!

  observe({
    if(input$sendSignal == 3)
      sendmail(from = "<te...@gmail.com>",

messages.subject: Re: Is there any way to select a row when DT is working on server side?
messages.subject_clean: Is there any way to select a row when DT is working on server side?
messages.body_plain:
Yeah! I found the solution understanding how the JS function works.

This code allows the user to select one row and shows its ID at the bottom. Pay attention, the selection is not visible on the table when the user changes page, this is because of the server side process. But at least you can have a reaction also on this situation.
I also have a code for multi-select, but it is making less sense when working on server side. Let me know if you need it.

Max

## DT Server Side

library(shiny)
library(DT)
library(data.table)
ID=seq(1,nrow(mtcars))
data=data.table(ID,mtcars)
shinyApp(
    ui = fluidPage(
        title = 'Server-side processing of DataTables, with Row Selector'
        ,fluidRow(uiOutput('info'))

        ,fluidRow(DT::dataTableOutput('tbl'))
        ,fluidRow(textOutput('log'))

        ,fluidRow(uiOutput('link'))

    ),
    server = function(input, output, session) {

        output$info=renderUI(h2('DT table Server Side with Row Selector'))

        output$tbl = DT::renderDataTable(
            datatable(data
                      ,server=TRUE
                      ,escape=FALSE

                      ,rownames = FALSE
                      ,options=list(
                          ajax = list(url = dataTableAjax(rowname=FALSE, session, data))  #must be present if server side, must have the 'data' frame used for the table
                      )
                      ,callback = JS(

                          "table.on('click.dt', 'tr', function() {
                                if ( $(this).hasClass('selected') ) {
                                    $(this).removeClass('selected');
                                }
                                else {
                                    table.$('tr.selected').removeClass('selected');
                                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                                }

                                Shiny.onInputChange('tbl_selected',

                                    table.rows('.selected').data().toArray());
                    });")

            )
        )
        output$link=renderUI(a('Documentation',href='https://rstudio.github.io/DT/server.html'))
        output$log=renderText(paste0('ID selected: ',paste(input$tbl_selected[1],collapse=',')))
    }
)

messages.subject_clean: Shiny not binding all outputs
messages.body_plain:
I have an app with custom outputs that are not working anymore with 0.12.  It is not a jsonlite issue.

My custom outputs are mustache templates rendered with the data passed from a shiny "renderTemplate" function.  Some of the divs containing these outputs are dynamically generated when the page loads (but not from R - this is a custom UI).  Sometimes shiny recognizes them as shiny bound outputs and sometimes it doesn't.  I can get around the problem if I increase the timeout on the timeout for initShiny.  But that is not a good solution.  In versions before 0.12 I could call Shiny.unbindAll() followed by Shiny.bindAll().  But in 0.12, Shiny.bindAll() still does not find all of the elements defined by the scope of my custom output, and it doesn't work.

Any idea on what might have changed or how I might get around this issue?

Not that it matters, but I don't think the unbindAll is necessary here; the unbindAll/bindAll pattern usually goes:

unbindAll(el);
// mutate el
bindAll(el);

bindAll is supposed to be smart enough to automatically skip any already-bound elements. I think.

Anyway... you said sometimes they're bound, sometimes they're not. Does that mean it's not deterministic? i.e. the same output might be bound sometimes, others not, with no code changes?

messages.subject: Re: How to access uploaded files by names in shiny
messages.subject_clean: How to access uploaded files by names in shiny
messages.body_plain:
I haven't read all the comments here fully so maybe this is redundant, but I do have a function that I've used exactly for this for quite some time and it seems to work for me. In general I prefer to keep the random filenames, and I only use this function if I really need the files to be named properly

#' When files get uploaded, their new filenames are gibberish.
#' This function renames all uploaded files to their original names
#' @param x The dataframe returned from a shiny::fileInput
fixUploadedFilesNames <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) {
    return()
  }

  oldNames = x$datapath
  newNames = file.path(dirname(x$datapath),
                       x$name)
  file.rename(from = oldNames, to = newNames)
  x$datapath <- newNames
  x
}

I'm just posting here to subscribe to the thread - I've also wondered about this :)

FWIW - I've asked Joe Cheng several months ago and he also seemed to think that there isn't really a good approach to testing yet and that selenium is probably a good choice

On Tuesday, 19 May 2015 08:13:10 UTC-7, ja...@prismfp.com wrote:
> Our company uses several shiny apps which we have written, both on our own servers and using the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> service.
>
> We are trying to put in place automated testing for these. At an absolute minimum we would like to know that the right app is running at the right URL, and that it loads correctly (not greyed out on load, no error console). Ideally we would like to check much more - for example we want to click through all tabs to see that they load correctly, do some basic input, and check the output. We want to know about both bugs in our code or infrastructure problems such as incorrect database details before our customers do.
>
> We have started writing selenium tests, both with RSelenium and selenium for Python. However we have found that writing good Selenium tests is tricky, and that a lot of work has to be done to get tests which are reasonably stable, and which give us meaningful results. Some of this seems to the normal work that Selenium requires to be used (ie finding all the right CSS selectors and checking the DOM after each UI interaction to check for elements which might have moved/disappeared/been replaced). Some of it seems to be related to the complexity of our pages and the Shiny UI elements, and some of it we think is unexpected behavior by Selenium. One example is that we have found it impossible in RSelenium to correctly interact with the Selectize Bootstrap widget in Shiny.
>
> Is Selenium the best approach and is RSelenium the best others have found to test Shiny? Is there anything that we should know about when trying to write Selenium tests for Shiny code? Should we change how we write our app code to make Selenium testing work better?
>
> I would be very happy to here from anyone who has any suggestions or can share there experiences, particularly if they have been successful in doing extensive automated testing of Shiny apps.
>
> Thanks ia,
> Jack Grahl
>

messages.subject: Re: running shiny from terminal
messages.subject_clean: running shiny from terminal
messages.body_plain:
Having to explicit load `methods` is a hassle for users (and confusing
to people who haven't encountered this before). I realize it's a quirk
of RScript, but I think it's a quirk that means package authors should
make the dependence on `methods` explicit.

Seems like it would be better to add `methods` to the "Depends: ..."
(e.g. like Hadley did for testthat in response to this issue:
https://github.com/hadley/testthat/issues/122).

According to this (http://r-pkgs.had.co.nz/description.html), adding
it to "Imports: ..." instead of "Depends: ..." should work for users
of R 3.2.0+.

On Wed, May 20, 2015 at 10:39 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> No, it's just what Rscript requires you to do. It's a well documented quirk
> of Rscript, it omits methods from the default package list for performance
> reasons.
>
> Sent from Outlook

messages.body_plain:
The motivation of not loading the methods package was to save some
time when starting up R. Turns out the time saved is about 0.05
seconds, and this 0.05 seconds have wasted so many people countless
hours. Yeah, this thing has been confusing for several years. Depends
won't work for R CMD check because when you load a package (e.g.
shiny::column), the Depends packages will not be attached. It can also
be problematic when another package imports a function from shiny, and
methods in Depends will also be ignored.

According to your reference to Hadley's book, it seems the problem has
been fixed, but I do not see a NEWS item in R 3.2.0. If it has really
been fixed, they should have been shouting from the rooftops in the
NEWS!

Regards,
Yihui

> > >
> > > unbindAll(el);
> > > // mutate el
> > > bindAll(el);
> > >
> > > bindAll is supposed to be smart enough to automatically skip any already-bound elements. I think.

messages.subject: Shiny renderUI selectInput returned NULL
messages.subject_clean: Shiny renderUI selectInput returned NULL
messages.body_plain:
Sorry (newbi here), I posted this to Stack Overflow (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/30378310/shiny-renderui-selectinput-returned-null),
but then discover this group, which I think is a better fit for this question.

I am trying to use a reactivity model with one input affecting several outputs as describe in the shiny cheat sheet. I need to use renderUI because the choices list is rendered dynamically (not shown in the example) However, during initialization selectInput returns NULL rather than the default value. After that first NULL value the input works as expected. I am new to shiny and might be doing something wrong.

This can be resolved by catching the NULL with an if  return statement, but there might be a better solution.

UPDATE: other controls unexpectedly returned not only NULL, but also NA after initialization.

See code below. See the console output, the first input returning NULL.
Listening on http://127.0.0.1:6211
 NULL
 chr "1"
 chr "2"
 chr "1"

library(shiny)

runApp(list(

  ui = bootstrapPage(
    fluidPage( uiOutput('ui.A')   )
  ),

  server = function(input, output){

    output$ui.A = renderUI({
      selectInput("A", label = h4("input A"),
                  choices = list(A_1=1, A_2=2),
                  selected = 1)
    })

    A.r <- reactive({input$A })

messages.subject: Should header/footer of "navbarPage" always be wrapped in "column"?
messages.subject_clean: Should header/footer of "navbarPage" always be wrapped in "column"?
messages.body_plain:
When using `navbarPage`, the header and footer are inserted inside an HTML "row". As a result of that, because bootstrap applies a -15px margin-left to rows, the header/footer content is misaligned with the content in tabs.
Bootstrap also says that "only columns may be immediate children of rows" (http://getbootstrap.com/css/#grid)

So I always wrap my header/footer arguments in a "column(12, ...)".  Since this seems to be mandatory, would it make sense to take care of that in shiny-core instead of us doing it manually? Or are there cases where it couldn't be right to auto-wrap the arguments in a column?

Example: the following is misaligned (and is "illegal" according to bootstrap")

runApp(shinyApp(
  ui = navbarPage(
    id = "test",
    title = "test",
    header = "this is a header",
    footer = "this is a footer",
    tabPanel("mytab", "this is a tab")
  ),
  server = function(input, output, session) {}
))

Replace footer/header with:

    header = column(12, "this is a header"),
    footer = column(12, "this is a footer"),

messages.body_plain:
Well if you want to reset absolutely everything and get back to the initial state of the app, then browser refresh is definitely a viable option. This is for when you want to reset a single input or a group of inputs. For example if you have several panels, and after submitting one, you want to reset its inputs.  Although even if you just have a form and you want to reset the inputs after submission, I'd argue it's more user friendly to reset the inputs rather than seeing the page refresh itself.

messages.subject_clean: Shiny testing - best practices and advice
messages.body_plain:
Following Dean's example ... I have only tried a few things with Rselenium and agree it is not particularly easy to use. One thing I have done is use 'regular' r-functions that are called from reactive functions as much as possible. That way I can at least test the 'regular' functions using testthat.

On Wednesday, May 20, 2015 at 5:00:24 PM UTC-7, Dean Attali wrote:
> I'm just posting here to subscribe to the thread - I've also wondered about this :)
>
> FWIW - I've asked Joe Cheng several months ago and he also seemed to think that there isn't really a good approach to testing yet and that selenium is probably a good choice
>
> On Tuesday, 19 May 2015 08:13:10 UTC-7, ja...@prismfp.com wrote:
> > Our company uses several shiny apps which we have written, both on our own servers and using the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> service.
> >
> > We are trying to put in place automated testing for these. At an absolute minimum we would like to know that the right app is running at the right URL, and that it loads correctly (not greyed out on load, no error console). Ideally we would like to check much more - for example we want to click through all tabs to see that they load correctly, do some basic input, and check the output. We want to know about both bugs in our code or infrastructure problems such as incorrect database details before our customers do.
> >
> > We have started writing selenium tests, both with RSelenium and selenium for Python. However we have found that writing good Selenium tests is tricky, and that a lot of work has to be done to get tests which are reasonably stable, and which give us meaningful results. Some of this seems to the normal work that Selenium requires to be used (ie finding all the right CSS selectors and checking the DOM after each UI interaction to check for elements which might have moved/disappeared/been replaced). Some of it seems to be related to the complexity of our pages and the Shiny UI elements, and some of it we think is unexpected behavior by Selenium. One example is that we have found it impossible in RSelenium to correctly interact with the Selectize Bootstrap widget in Shiny.
> >
> > Is Selenium the best approach and is RSelenium the best others have found to test Shiny? Is there anything that we should know about when trying to write Selenium tests for Shiny code? Should we change how we write our app code to make Selenium testing work better?
> >
> > I would be very happy to here from anyone who has any suggestions or can share there experiences, particularly if they have been successful in doing extensive automated testing of Shiny apps.
> >
> > Thanks ia,
> > Jack Grahl
> >

messages.subject: Re: sliderInput formatting
messages.subject_clean: sliderInput formatting
messages.body_plain:
Regarding the main question: that's strange, I haven't noticed that before.  It seems like it's treating the value to the right of the decimal as an integer, and inserts commas as if it was a regular number. It looks like `sliderInput` has a `sep` parameter that is a comma by default, so if you supply `sep = ""`, it will fix that.  BUT that will also affect the number to the left of the decimal, so if you have numbers that are greater than 1000, they will not be formatted with commas.  Seems like a bug to me. Maybe someone else can shed some more light on this.

 sliderInput("xbar", NULL, 7.4945, 9.4066, 8.45, .03, animate=list(interval=2000), width="150px", sep = "")

On Monday, 25 May 2015 19:50:55 UTC-7, Richard Heiberger wrote:
> This example
>
> shinyApp(
>     ui = sliderInput("xbar", NULL, 7.4945, 9.4066, 8.45, .03, animate=list(interval=2000), width="150px"),
>   server=function(input, output) {
>   })
>
>
> produces a slider with limits
> 7.4,945  and 9.4,066
> where it is apparently counting to the left from the end of the number.
>
> How can I tell it to suppress the "," and use
> 7.4945  and 9.4066
>
>
> And I don't really want this, but how can I tell it to put the ","
> counting to the right of the decimal point so it would give
> 7.494,5  and 9.406,6
>
> Rich
>

messages.body_plain:
It's definitely doable, here's a rewrite of your app. Note that I moved the select inputs to be defined in the server and rendered as `renderUI` instead having them awkwardly defined in UI with random choices and then populating them with normal choices later.

runApp(shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(

    sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(

        # Select Studies

        uiOutput("studyIdSelect"),

        # Select Cases
        uiOutput("caseIdSelect")

      ),

    mainPanel(
      verbatimTextOutput('Studies_values'),
      tableOutput('Cases_values')

    ))

  ),
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    ## Select Studies
    library(cgdsr)
    cgds <- CGDS("http://www.cbioportal.org/public-portal/")
    Studies <- getCancerStudies(cgds)

    output$studyIdSelect <- renderUI({
      selectizeInput('StudiesID', 'Studies 1', choices = Studies[, 1], multiple = TRUE)

    })

    output$Studies_values <- renderPrint({
      list(List_Studies = input$StudiesID)
    })

    output$caseIdSelect <- renderUI({
      Cases <- lapply(input$StudiesID, function(x) getCaseLists(cgds, x))
      Cases <- do.call(rbind, Cases)

      selectizeInput('CasesID', 'Cases 1', choices = Cases[, 1] , multiple = TRUE)

    })

    output$Cases_values<- renderPrint({
      list(List_Cases = input$CasesID)
    })
  }

))

The main bit of interest is

      Cases <- lapply(input$StudiesID, function(x) getCaseLists(cgds, x))
      Cases <- do.call(rbind, Cases)

Basically, whenever studies are chosen, we go through all the study ids, get all the cases for each study id, and then bind together the resulting dataframe

messages.subject: Re: How can I close a session from within the session?
messages.subject_clean: How can I close a session from within the session?
messages.body_plain:
The Shiny window is not opened from a JavaScript call. It's either from the user navigating to it (Shiny Server case) or the operating system invoking the browser (local R session case).

It is standard to log out, what's not standard is for the window/tab to be closed. Almost every website works this way--after you log out, it sends you to a different page, it doesn't close the window/tab.

No matter how the session ends, be it timeout, accidental disconnect, whatever, onSessionEnded will be called on the server side (unless the R process itself crashes, obviously then we don't get a chance to clean up). Keep in mind though, that when onSessionEnded is called, you can clean up anything on the server but it's too late to communicate with the client--onSessionEnded means the connection has already been broken.

Your checkFunction would be some kind of cheap-to-execute expression that would change when the data has changed, for example the result of the query "select MAX(CHANGED) from DF_JOURNALPTI4" (I'm just assuming that CHANGED is a timestamp field).

The valueFunction would be the query to get the actual data you want (in this case, getPTI4Journal).

You also provide a polling interval. reactivePoll will automatically execute your checkFunction once per polling interval, and if the returned value changes, it will execute the full valueFunction.

The return value of reactivePoll is a reactive expression (e.g. you call it like a function to retrieve its value) that represents the most recent valueFunction result.

I hope that makes sense...

messages.subject: Re: Updating an input and using the new value immediately
messages.subject_clean: Updating an input and using the new value immediately
messages.body_plain:
Perhaps I don't understand your question, but this does not seem complicated.  updateTextInput returns when it has sent a message to the client, telling it to update the text box. You can see this in the shiny code, here: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/89bc7efbca09a068dd3757dd798248eaac06e80c/R/update-input.R
The textInput will not change until that message has been received by the client.  You will then get a message back from the client, telling you that input$time has changed, but you don't have an observer so you won't know when that happens. If time on the server is what you want, you can write this:
> observeEvent(input$update, {
>      temp <- getTime()
> > updateTextInput(session, "time", value = temp)
>      cat(temp, "\n")
>     })

If you want the time on the client, I think you have to write a javascript function as part of ui.R.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny server with bigger data - in memory
messages.subject_clean: Shiny server with bigger data - in memory
messages.body_plain:
The Shiny Server config directives app_init_timeout and app_idle_timeout may be relevant:
http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#application-timeouts

They don't make the startup any faster, but app_init_timeout can prevent long startup from causing an error, and app_idle_timeout can be used to prevent expensive-to-start R process from being retired.

Ideally though, you would find a way to load less data, perhaps by doing some kind of summarizing/aggregation, and save that as your .RData or .rds file to be loaded at startup. Shiny can only ever be as fast as the instructions you give it, and loading dozens of GB of data directly into memory is going to take time.

This is expected behavior. When the client initially connects, the selectInput "A" does not exist.

But you can use validate(need(input$xxxxx, message=FALSE)) too, in any reactive expression or output or observer where you don't want to proceed unless input$xxxxx is non-NULL.

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Joe for this clarification.

I understand that we need time (R time, not shiny) to load the data in memory, but why should it be for every user ? And not only once and for all with shiny server.

> The Shiny Server config directives app_init_timeout and app_idle_timeout may be relevant:
> http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#application-timeouts

> They don't make the startup any faster, but app_init_timeout can prevent long startup from causing an error, and app_idle_timeout can be used to prevent expensive-to-start R process from being retired.

messages.subject: Re: managing multiple leaflet maps with tabPanels
messages.subject_clean: managing multiple leaflet maps with tabPanels
messages.body_plain:
I think the problem here is that when a Leaflet map (or any HTML element) is hidden, its size is 0 pixels by 0 pixels. Leaflet isn't designed to work well when you send it commands (like fitBounds) while it's sized like that. We tried to work around this problem in some scenarios by delaying rendering the map until it's actually visible--but I didn't take into account leafletProxy(), so I'm not sure what other bugs are still lurking when you use leafletProxy on a hidden map.

Those are things we should try to figure out before the Leaflet package goes to CRAN. But in the meantime, I think you'd be better served by reorganizing the UI to have a single map, if that's your intention. I'd create a UI where only the inputs are in tabs, maybe like this:

library(shiny)
library(leaflet)

ui <- fluidPage(
  h1("My app"),
  fluidRow(
    column(4,
      tabsetPanel(
        tabPanel("A",
          "Controls"
        ),
        tabPanel("B",
          "More controls"
        )
      )
    ),
    column(8,
      leafletOutput("map", height = 600)
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$map <- renderLeaflet({
    leaflet() %>% addTiles()
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: Re: removeShape problem shiny leaflet
messages.subject_clean: removeShape problem shiny leaflet
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

You forgot to put a layerId when you create your rectangle, and you need it to remove it in removeShape.

So you need to have something like this :

############# red box
observeEvent(input$red, {
  if(input$red==TRUE) {
    leafletProxy("map", session) %>%
      addRectangles(
        lng1=-119.456554, lat1=35.078039,
        lng2=-118.436383, lat2=34.062717,

        layerId = "red",

        fillColor = "red")
  }
})

> I'm having trouble getting my leaflet app to work correctly in shiny.  Specifically, I would like to be able to turn on/off layers using the check box.  The layers turn on fine but do not turn off correctly (i.e., disappear when unchecking the box).  For a single layer, I can work around this using the clearShapes() function.  But I want to be able to display multiple layers and turn on and off as desired using the removeShape function. I don't know if I'm doing this incorrectly or some other approach is better.  A reproducible example is below
>
>
> library(leaflet)
> library(shiny)
> app = shinyApp(
>   ui = fluidPage(checkboxInput("blue", "blue", TRUE),
>                  checkboxInput("red", "red", FALSE),
>                 leafletOutput('map')),
>   server = function(input, output, session) {
>     map = leaflet() %>% addTiles() %>% setView(-119, 34.57, zoom = 7) #%>%
>
>
>

>

>         leafletProxy("map", session) %>%
>           addRectangles(
>             lng1=-118.456554, lat1=34.078039,
>             lng2=-117.436383, lat2=33.062717,
>             fillColor = "blue")
>             }
>           })
> ############# blue box end
>
>
> ############# red box
> observeEvent(input$red, {
>   if(input$red==TRUE) {
>     leafletProxy("map", session) %>%
>       addRectangles(
>         lng1=-119.456554, lat1=35.078039,
>         lng2=-118.436383, lat2=34.062717,
>         fillColor = "red")
>   }
> })
>
>
>   observeEvent(input$red, {

I've something like this:

navbarPage(
title = "title",
    id = "shinyNav",
    collapsible = T,
    header=singleton(tags$head(includeScript('google-analytics.js'))),
    tabPanel("tab1",
             includeScript("track.js")
            ),
    tabPanel("tab2",
             includeScript("track.js")
            )
)

where my track script is

ga('send', 'pageview');

However, i cannot find the corresponding tabs showing up under contents in the GA dashboard. Could someone shed some light on how to properly track the different tab clicks structured in a navbarPage please? Thank you in advance.

messages.subject: Re: shiny mobile version with navbar fixed-bottom while desktop navbar on top
messages.subject_clean: shiny mobile version with navbar fixed-bottom while desktop navbar on top
messages.body_plain:
This sounds like a CSS issue more than a shiny topic.  Are you familiar with CSS, especially with the `media` directive that can be used to control the look on mobile vs desktop or small vs big screen?
For example, you could add a certain class to all the navbar icons and the navbar text, and selectively choose to show or hide it depending on what device is being used.  Google "responsive css" or "css for mobile vs desktop" to learn how to do this.
